steps: Circle :g:`( A B C D ) <g1:( A B C D )>`

In :g:`( A B C D ) <g1:( A B C D )>` inscribe side :g:`/ A C / <g1:/ A C />` of equilateral triangle :g:`< A C D > <g1:< A C D >>` (@fn(IV.2)) and side :g:`/ A B / <g1:/ A B />` of regular pentagon (@fn(IV.11))

Of 15 equal parts of :g:`( A B C D ) <g1:( A B C D )>`, arc :g:`( A B C ) <g1:( A B C )>` (⅓ of circle) contains 5 and arc :g:`( A B ) <g1:( A B )>` (⅕ of circle) contains 3 → remainder arc :g:`( B C ) <g1:( B C )>` contains 5 − 3 = 2 parts

Bisecting :g:`( B C ) <g1:( B C )>` at :g:`E <g1:E>` makes each of :g:`( B E ) <g1:( B E )>`, :g:`( E C ) <g1:( E C )>` equal to 1/15 of :g:`( A B C D ) <g1:( A B C D )>`; fitting chords equal to :g:`/ B E / <g1:/ B E />`, :g:`/ E C / <g1:/ E C />` continuously around :g:`( A B C D ) <g1:( A B C D )>` inscribes the regular fifteen-angled figure :g:`< A B E C D > <g1:< A B E C D >>`
